title: Inclusive interview scheduling and accessibility flow
content:
Purpose:
This playbook standardizes how People Ops and recruiting coordinate interview scheduling with a focus on accessibility, timezone equity, and candidate dignity. It is designed to reduce friction for candidates who request accommodations (disability, neurodiversity, travel, caregiving constraints), ensure consistent interviewer experience, and document decisions for auditability.

Principles (short):
- Candidate agency: offer clear choices and default to lower-barrier options.
- Transparency: capture accommodations in the candidate record and share only what is necessary with interviewers.
- Timezone fairness: provide slots that respect local business hours for candidate region where possible.
- Minimal disruption: prefer asynchronous work samples where live formats create barriers.
- Privacy & need-to-know: only include accommodation details with interviewer panel if required for performance of the interview.

High-level flow (recruiter / People Ops):
1) Intake & preference capture (within 24 hours of screen):
   - Ask: preferred interview windows (morning/afternoon/evening local time), timezone, phone or video, assistive tech (closed captions, relay, screen reader), sign language needs, repeated short breaks, sensory considerations.
   - Use the standardized candidate intake form (link above). Save entries in the candidate record.
2) Offer scheduling options (within 48 hours of intake):
   - Provide at least three time slots across two different days that fit both the core interviewers and candidate preferences.
   - Include at least one asynchronous alternative (take-home task or recorded response).
3) Accommodation confirmation:
   - Confirm any requested accommodations in writing and the People Ops accessibility owner (Priya or backup) triages if complex.
   - If an interpreter or live captioner is required, book at least 72 hours in advance.
4) Calendar invites & metadata:
   - Invite should include: explicit duration, break windows, clear joining instructions, signpost the accommodation note (e.g., "Candidate has requested live captioning — captions will be enabled in the call").
   - Add a single-line organizer note in the invite private description: "Accommodations requested: [brief non-sensitive note]". Do not paste medical details.
5) Interviewer prep (48–24 hours before):
   - Send interviewer prep with: how to run inclusive interviews, how to enable captions/recordings, what behaviorally anchored rubric to use, and what pieces of the candidate record are relevant (e.g., timeline constraints).
6) Day-of contingency:
   - If assistive tooling fails (e.g., captioning drops), switch to the backup: phone call with simultaneous chat notes, or reschedule to nearest available slot with candidate consent.

Detailed guidelines and checklists:
A. Scheduling checklist for recruiters (checkbox-style text for copy/paste):
   - [ ] Completed candidate intake: timezone, preferred windows, tool preferences
   - [ ] Flagged any accommodation requests in candidate record
   - [ ] Offered at least 3 slots + 1 async alternative
   - [ ] Booked interpreter/CA 72h ahead if needed
   - [ ] Prepared calendar invite with accommodation note in private description
   - [ ] Linked interview rubric and evaluation form in invite
   - [ ] Confirmed that all interviewers have access to required assistive tech or instructions

B. Accessibility logistics quick reference for common requests:
   - Live captions / CART: use built-in captions (Zoom/Meet) where possible; if accuracy is critical, book CART vendor. Plan 72h lead time.
   - ASL/BSL interpreter: coordinate vendor and include interpreter email in invite. Book 72–120h ahead for scheduling flexibility.
   - Screen reader / NVDA guidance: provide candidate with materials in accessible format (text, alt text for images) before the interview.
   - Neurodiversity needs (processing time, sensory breaks): add 5–10 minute buffer between interviews; offer written questions in advance if requested.
   - Travel/accommodation: provide explicit travel guidance, reimbursements policy link, and local contact.

C. Interview format decision matrix (when to use async vs live):
   - Asynchronous preferred when: candidate requests live-video accommodation, timezone >8 hours offset, or recorded sample is a fairer measure (writing / take-home task).
   - Live preferred when: role requires live communication testing (customer-facing, sales, live pair-programming) and candidate does not object.

D. Email / message templates (copy-paste editable)
   - Scheduling offering (short):
     "Thanks — would any of these windows work for you? Option A: Tue 10–11am your local time; Option B: Wed 5–6pm your local time; Option C: Thu 9–10am. If none work, happy to send more options. We can provide live captions, an interpreter, or an asynchronous alternative — which would you prefer?
     
     Best,
     [Recruiter name]"

   - Accommodation confirmation (sensitive, short):
     "Thanks for letting us know. We confirm we will provide: [list of accommodations]. Our team will handle the logistics. If anything changes, we will check in with you.
     
     — [Recruiter name], People Ops"

   - Reschedule due to tech failure (day-of):
     "Apologies — we hit a tech issue with captions for today. Would you prefer we (A) switch to phone + chat notes now, or (B) reschedule to a time we can guarantee captioning? Please let me know which you prefer and I’ll act immediately.
     
     — [Recruiter name]"

E. Interviewer-facing inclusion tips (to paste in prep doc):
   - Use the candidate’s preferred name and pronouns.
   - Read questions aloud and allow extra think-time before expecting an answer.
   - If a candidate requests written follow-ups, honor it — treat as equivalent evidence.
   - Do not ask about medical conditions; ask about what adjustments will make the interview fair.
   - Focus on behaviorally anchored evidence; avoid hypotheticals that depend on sensory or rapid-fire tasks unless necessary.

F. Recording, note-taking, and privacy policy:
   - Recording: default is not to record live interviews. If required (e.g., for quality calibration), obtain candidate consent and store in private HR folder.
   - Notes: Store accommodation details in the private candidate record with access limited to People Ops and the hiring manager.

Operational roles and SLAs:
- Recruiter: first reply to scheduling intake within 24 hours, send confirmed invite within 48 hours.
- People Ops accessibility owner: acknowledge any non-standard accommodation request within 24 hours and propose logistics within 48 hours.
- Hiring manager: confirm interviewer panel fits accommodation needs within 48 hours of invite.

Tracking & minimal audit log fields (to add to ATS custom fields):
- accommodation_requested (yes/no)
- accommodation_type (short list: captioning, interpreter, asynchronous, other)
- accommodation_confirmed_by (initials)
- accommodation_booked_at (YYYY-MM-DD)
- scheduling_offered_slots (comma separated localized datetimes)

Decision notes and escalation guide:
- If the requested accommodation appears to require major schedule rework (>3 calendar changes) or budget for vendors, escalate to People Ops lead (Priya) for approval.
- For repeated cancellations attributable to vendor failures, move to internal captioning + asynchronous fallback and debrief vendor performance with procurement.

Equity considerations / legal reminder:
- We comply with local disability laws and EEO requirements. Offer equivalent evaluation paths and do not disadvantage candidates who use accommodations. Document decisions and maintain evidence used in hiring decisions for 2 years where applicable.

Open questions & follow-ups (work-in-progress):
- Define a short list of preferred captioning & interpreter vendors and procurement block-book rates.
- ATS UI changes to surface accommodation fields earlier in workflow.
- Guidance for panel interviews across multiple timezones (split panels, repeat panels, or use recorded segments).

Appendix: vendor checklist & basic rates (internal note):
- CART vendor A: English live captioning, 120 USD/hr, 3hr minimum.
- ASL vendor B: 85 USD/hr, flexible scheduling.
- Backup internal captioning: use Google Meet live captions (lower accuracy) — set candidate expectation.

Owner & next steps:
- Owner: Priya Nambiar (People Ops accessibility owner).
- Next milestone: finalize vendor list and procurement SOW by 2026-02-01.

Document change log (high level):
- 2025-10-02: initial draft created by Priya
- 2026-01-15: updates for async format guidance and vendor SLA windows

Notes to reviewer:
- This is intended to be a lightweight operational playbook for day-to-day recruiters. Please flag anything that will create legal or procurement dependencies.
